stories.title: Venezuela says 131 political prisoners freed amid post-Maduro talks
stories.summary: As detainees granted ‘alternative’ to imprisonment, US welcomes release as a crucial step for Venezuela’s reconciliation process. Venezuela says it has freed 131 people considered political prisoners, in a sign of progress for national reconciliation following the United States’ removal of former President Nicolas Maduro. Those released had been granted “alternative measures from incarceration” under the Program for Peace and Democratic Coexistence, the country’s interim government said on Friday. Opposition movement Vente Venezuela said it had independently verified the release of 43 detainees, and the Foro Penal rights group, which advocates for the release of alleged political prisoners, said “at least 40” had been freed. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the recent release of more than 130 political prisoners in Venezuela is “a crucial step for the nation’s reconciliation process”. Since the US overthrew and detained Maduro on January 3 this year, 1,046 Venezuelans have been released, Rubio added on X. Venezuela is now being governed by Maduro’s former deputy, Delcy Rodriguez, with significant influence from Washington. Former prisoners were seen reuniting with their families in emotional scenes outside El Rodeo. I prison in Guatire, 50 kilometres (31 miles) east of the capital Caracas. Foro Penal said that 17 women had been freed on Friday, including one accused of participating in an assassination plot against Maduro. It earlier said 391 political prisoners remained behind bars as of August 10. Opposition figure Juan Pablo Guanipa welcomed the releases but demanded that all political prisoners be freed.

stories.title: Coalition split on Andrew Bragg speech as South Australian senator Andrew McLachlan urges colleagues to ‘follow his lead’
stories.summary: Senior colleagues dismiss Bragg’s migration figures as ‘personal views’ while others say critical response is an ‘overreaction’ Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Liberal senator Andrew McLachlan has publicly backed Andrew Bragg and urged colleagues to “follow his lead” after a public speech that has split colleagues and triggered a rebuke from opposition leader, Angus Taylor. At the National Press Club on Wednesday, Bragg announced a policy to slash the national construction code and suggested net overseas migration should be dropped from the current level of about 300,000 to below 180,000 a year to keep pace with new housing builds. stories.title: Houthi spokesman says 'Saudi warships and mercenaries' targeted
stories.summary: Houthi spokesman says 'Saudi warships and mercenaries' targeted Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree has said the rebels “targeted concentrations and weapons belonging to the Saudi enemy”. In a statement carried by Press TV, Saree said the “servicemen targeted warships belonging to its (Riyadh’s) tools and mercenaries in the al-Mokha area, using a large number of ballistic missiles”. “The strike was precise, and the operation resulted in the destruction of the boats and weapons, and the death and injury of dozens among the Saudi enemy's concentrations,” he said, according to the statement.
